mainTopic: מעילה in הקדש חמץ during פסח, and the rules for mixtures of חמץ during and after פסח (רב, שמואל, רבי יוחנן)
overview: The amud first finishes a dispute about someone who uses חמץ belonging to הקדש during פסח: did he commit מעילה or not? Three explanations are given. רב יוסף says it depends on whether something that will only be worth money later (דבר הגורם לממון) already counts as money. רב אחא בר יעקב says future value counts for everyone, and the dispute follows רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון about whether חמץ is permitted after פסח. The גמרא challenges him with another statement of his, and answers that he retracted it. רב אשי says future value does not count for anyone, and the dispute follows רבי יוסי הגלילי and the רבנן about benefit from חמץ during פסח. Then a new topic begins: a mixture with a small amount of חמץ in it. רב is strict during פסח, partly by a גזירה, and after פסח he forbids the same kind, following רבי יהודה. שמואל is more lenient, and רבי יוחנן measures everything by נותן טעם during פסח. Both permit everything after פסח, following רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רב יוסף's version: the dispute is about future value
steps.stepSummary: A version in the name of רב יוסף: everyone agrees קדשים may not be redeemed to feed dogs. The dispute is whether a דבר הגורם לממון counts as money.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaching was taught in the name of רב יוסף in this wording: everyone agrees that we may not redeem sacred animals in order to feed them to dogs. Here the two sides disagree about whether something that leads to money counts as money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new version of the explanation of the dispute about using הקדש חמץ on פסח, taught in the name of רב יוסף. In this version, the question about redeeming קדשים for dog food is no longer the point of the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During פסח the חמץ cannot be used for benefit, so right now it is worthless. But after פסח it may become usable again and be worth money. The question is whether that future worth already counts as 'value' now, which would make the person liable for מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or ruling (here, the dispute being discussed)
Redeeming sacred items (swapping their holiness onto money)
An item that is not worth money now but leads to money (or to a loss of money)

steps.whyThisMatters: The principle of דבר הגורם לממון is a well-known disputed principle that shows up in many places in ש"ס. Here it is applied to מעילה.

phrases.english: this teaching
phrases.notes: Continues from the previous דף, where someone 'taught' (מתני) this teaching in a different version.

phrases.english: in the name of Rav Yosef
with this wording:
that everyone agrees
one may not redeem consecrated items
in order to feed them to dogs,
and here they disagree about this:
whether an item that leads to money
is considered like money.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף בְּהָא לִישָּׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second version of the explanation of the dispute that began on the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All agree that קדשים are not redeemed for dog food. The dispute is whether דבר הגורם לממון counts as ממון.

steps.title: Matching each side to the principle
steps.stepSummary: The one who says מעל holds that future value counts as money. The one who says לא מעל holds that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says he committed מעילה holds that something that leads to money counts as money. The one who says he did not commit מעילה holds that something that leads to money does not count as money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out which side of the dispute holds which view about דבר הגורם לממון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to מעל, the חמץ will be worth money after פסח, so it already counts as valuable now, and using it is מעילה. According to לא מעל, only present value counts. Since the חמץ is worthless during פסח, there is no מעילה.

phrases.english: The one who said he misused,
holds: an item that leads to money
is considered like money.
And the one who said he did not misuse,
holds: an item that leads to money
is not considered like money.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר מָעַל, קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the principle from step 1 to each side of the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעל = דבר הגורם לממון כממון דמי. לא מעל = לאו כממון דמי.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב: the dispute follows רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב says everyone agrees future value counts. The dispute is whether this חמץ is permitted after פסח, which is the argument between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: everyone agrees that something that leads to money counts as money. Here they argue along the lines of the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון. The one who says he did not commit מעילה follows רבי יהודה. The one who says he did follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא offers a completely different explanation of the dispute. He moves it away from the money principle and over to the תנאים's argument about חמץ after פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that חמץ that existed during פסח stays forbidden forever. So this חמץ will never have value, and there is no מעילה. רבי שמעון holds that it becomes permitted after פסח, so it has future value, and that future value counts. Therefore מעל.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who offers an alternative explanation

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In רב יוסף's version, everyone assumes the חמץ will have value after פסח, and the argument is whether future value counts. In רב אחא בר יעקב's version, everyone agrees future value counts, and the argument is whether the חמץ will have any value at all.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
Everyone agrees that an item that leads to money
is considered like money,
and here, in the dispute
of Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon they disagree:
The one who said he did not misuse
follows Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה: חמץ that was around during פסח is forbidden forever.

phrases.english: And the one who said he misused
follows Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון: such חמץ is permitted after פסח.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the idea that the dispute is about דבר הגורם לממון and puts forward a different underlying cause.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All agree דבר הגורם לממון כממון דמי. לא מעל follows רבי יהודה, and מעל follows רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Challenge from רב אחא בר יעקב's own statement about רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: But רב אחא בר יעקב himself said that רבי יהודה learns the eating prohibition from the seeing prohibition. That would make הקדש חמץ permitted after פסח even according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't רב אחא בר יעקב the one who said that רבי יהודה learns the rules of eating leaven from the rules of seeing leaven?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אחא בר יעקב's explanation by pointing to another statement he made elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition of seeing חמץ (בל יראה) applies only to your own חמץ, not to חמץ of הקדש. If רבי יהודה learns eating from seeing, then הקדש חמץ is not forbidden after פסח even by רבי יהודה. If so, even רבי יהודה would hold that it has value and that there is מעילה, so the dispute cannot follow רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaven of eating (the prohibition against eating חמץ)
Leaven of seeing (the prohibition of בל יראה, which applies only to one's own חמץ)

phrases.english: But isn't it Rav Acha bar Yaakov
who said
that Rabbi Yehuda derives
leaven of eating
from leaven of seeing!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב הוּא דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 3 using a contradiction within רב אחא בר יעקב's own statements.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's claim that לא מעל follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יהודה learns eating from seeing, הקדש חמץ is permitted after פסח even for him. So it has value, and לא מעל cannot follow רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב retracted his earlier view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב אחא בר יעקב retracted his earlier statement about רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אחא בר יעקב retracted that statement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying רב אחא בר יעקב changed his mind and no longer holds that earlier statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once he retracted, he holds like רבא: according to רבי יהודה, all חמץ that existed during פסח is forbidden afterward, including הקדש חמץ. That keeps his explanation in step 3 working.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two explanations of the dispute about מעילה in הקדש חמץ on פסח. רב יוסף: it depends on whether דבר הגורם לממון counts as money. רב אחא בר יעקב: future value counts for everyone, and the dispute follows רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון about חמץ after פסח. He retracted his other statement about רבי יהודה to make this work.

phrases.english: Rather, he retracted
Rav Acha bar Yaakov, from that statement.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הֲדַר בֵּיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב מֵהַהִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction: the אמורא withdrew his conflicting statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed רב אחא בר יעקב still held that רבי יהודה learns eating from seeing.
steps.terutzMaskana: He retracted that statement, so according to רבי יהודה הקדש חמץ is forbidden after פסח and has no value.

steps.title: רב אשי links the dispute to רבי יוסי הגלילי and the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says everyone agrees that אין פודין and that a דבר הגורם לממון is not money. The dispute about מעילה depends on whether חמץ may be used for benefit during פסח. That is the argument between רבי יוסי הגלילי and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: everyone agrees that we do not redeem קדשים to feed dogs. Everyone also agrees that something that only leads to money later is not counted as money. Here they argue about the same thing that רבי יוסי הגלילי and the רבנן argue about. The one who says he did מעילה holds like רבי יוסי. The one who says he did not do מעילה holds like the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a third explanation of the dispute about eating הקדש חמץ on פסח. He moves the whole argument to the question of whether חמץ is allowed for benefit during פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף (step 1) said the dispute is about future value, and רב אחא בר יעקב (step 3) said it is about whether the חמץ is allowed after פסח. רב אשי says that everyone agrees future value does not count, so only the חמץ's value right now matters. According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, חמץ may be used for benefit during פסח, so it has value now and there is מעילה. According to the רבנן it is forbidden for benefit, so it is worth nothing now and there is no מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: A late אמורא who often gives the final explanation of a sugya
A תנא who holds that חמץ may be used for benefit during פסח
He committed מעילה, meaning he misused הקדש

steps.whatToRemember: There are three explanations of the מעילה dispute. רב יוסף says it is about future value. רב אחא בר יעקב says it is about whether the חמץ is allowed after פסח. רב אשי says it is about whether חמץ is allowed for benefit during פסח, which is the dispute between רבי יוסי הגלילי and the רבנן.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי agrees with רב יוסף's first half (אין פודין). However, he rejects the idea that the dispute is about a דבר הגורם לממון. In his view, everyone agrees it is NOT money.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Everyone agrees that one does not redeem (consecrated animals to feed dogs),
and an item that (only later) brings about money
is not considered like money,
and here, in the dispute
of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili and the Rabbis, they disagree.
phrases.notes: The dispute is whether חמץ is permitted for benefit during פסח.

phrases.english: The one who said he misused (הקדש) holds like Rabbi Yosei.
phrases.notes: The חמץ has benefit-value now, so it is worth money.

phrases.english: And the one who said he did not misuse holds like the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: The חמץ is forbidden for benefit now, so it is worthless.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אֲמַר: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא — אֵין פּוֹדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב אחא בר יעקב's approach is defended (step 5), רב אשי offers a different reason for the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees a דבר הגורם לממון is not money. The מעילה dispute follows the dispute between רבי יוסי הגלילי and the רבנן over benefit from חמץ during פסח.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the סוגיא about הקדש חמץ. It ties the question of מעילה directly to the basic question of whether there is a benefit prohibition on חמץ during פסח.

steps.title: רב's rule for leavened bread mixed into other food
steps.stepSummary: רב rules on mixtures of חמץ. During פסח, a mixture is forbidden whether the חמץ is mixed with its own kind or another kind. After פסח, it is forbidden with its own kind and permitted with another kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: if חמץ gets mixed in during its time (פסח), the mixture is forbidden, whether it was mixed with the same kind of food or a different kind. If it gets mixed in after its time, it is forbidden when mixed with the same kind and permitted when mixed with a different kind.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts here. רב gives a four-part rule about when a mixture containing חמץ is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule has two variables. The first is time: during פסח or after it. The second is the type of food it is mixed with: the same kind or a different kind. Only one of the four combinations is permitted: after פסח, mixed with a different kind. The גמרא will next ask what size of mixture רב is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: In its time, meaning during פסח when חמץ is forbidden
Not in its time, meaning after פסח
Mixed with its own kind of food
Mixed with a different kind of food

phrases.english: Rav said:
Leavened bread during its time (Passover),

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּמִינוֹ בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִינוֹ — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: whether (mixed) with its own type or with another type, is forbidden.
Not during its time: with its own type, it is forbidden;
with another type, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: חָמֵץ בִּזְמַנּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. It moves from מעילה to the rules for mixtures of חמץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During פסח, a mixture of חמץ is always forbidden. After פסח, it is forbidden with its own kind and permitted with a different kind.

steps.title: What amount of leavened bread is רב talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case רב means. If the חמץ is enough to give taste (נותן טעם), why would it be permitted after פסח with a different kind? It gives taste!
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If you say there is enough חמץ to give taste, then how can it be permitted after פסח when mixed with a different kind? It gives taste!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which amount of חמץ רב is talking about. It tests the first possibility, an amount that gives taste, and shows that it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חמץ can be tasted in the food, the mixture should be forbidden. This makes the ruling 'after פסח, different kind, permitted' impossible to understand. So רב cannot be talking about an amount that gives taste.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
Gives taste, meaning there is enough of the forbidden food to be tasted in the mixture

phrases.english: With what are we dealing?
If you say it is where it gives flavor,
(then) not during its time, with another type, is it permitted?
But it gives flavor!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִילֵימָא בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what case רב's rule refers to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What amount of חמץ in the mixture is רב talking about?
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility that רב means an amount that gives taste.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the חמץ gives taste, the mixture should be forbidden even after פסח with a different kind. That contradicts רב's ruling that it is permitted.

steps.title: רב is talking about a tiny amount
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב is talking about a tiny amount (משהו) of חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we are dealing with a tiny amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the answer: the case is a tiny, untastable amount of חמץ. Next, it will show how each part of רב's rule fits this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only a משהו, the ruling 'after פסח, different kind, permitted' makes sense, because nothing can be tasted. Now the stricter rulings need explaining: why would even a tiny amount forbid the mixture in the other cases?

keyTerms.meaning: With any tiny amount at all

phrases.english: Rather, (it is dealing) with any amount.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּמַשֶּׁהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 after the 'gives taste' option was rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב is talking about a mixture with only a tiny amount of חמץ.

steps.title: The first half of רב's rule fits his general view on mixtures
steps.stepSummary: During פסח, a tiny amount forbids the mixture with any kind of food. This fits רב's general view, which he shares with שמואל: for all Torah prohibitions, the same kind is forbidden even by a tiny amount, and a different kind is forbidden only when it gives taste.
steps.simpleTranslation: During פסח, חמץ forbids the mixture whether it is mixed with the same kind or a different kind. רב follows his own reasoning here. רב and שמואל both say: for all prohibitions in the Torah, when mixed with the same kind, even a tiny amount forbids it; when mixed with a different kind, it is forbidden only if it gives taste.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through רב's rule clause by clause. It shows that the 'same kind' part matches רב's well-known general rule about forbidden mixtures, which he holds together with שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and שמואל hold that a forbidden food mixed with the same kind forbids the mixture even in a tiny amount. So 'during פסח, same kind, forbidden' fits easily. This general rule does not explain why a tiny amount forbids a different kind during פסח. Normally that needs taste, so חמץ during פסח is stricter than usual, and the גמרא will deal with that next.
steps.confusionAlert: רב and שמואל's general rule only explains the same-kind case. During פסח, חמץ forbids a different kind even with a tiny amount, which is stricter than the general rule. This source does not explain the 'different kind' half. Step 11 explains it.

phrases.english: Leavened bread during its time,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּמִינוֹ בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִינוֹ אָסוּר,
phrases.english: whether with its own type or with another type, is forbidden,
Rav follows his own reasoning,
as Rav and Shmuel both say:
All prohibitions in the Torah,
with its own type, (are forbidden) with any amount;
with another type, (only) when it gives flavor.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that we know the case is a משהו (step 9), the גמרא explains the first clause of רב's rule using his general view.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that during פסח, a tiny amount of חמץ in a mixture forbids it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared statement of רב and שמואל: for all Torah prohibitions, the same kind is forbidden even in a tiny amount, and a different kind is forbidden only when it gives taste.
steps.whyThisMatters: The general rule of רב and שמואל (מין במינו במשהו, שלא במינו בנותן טעם) is a basic principle in the laws of mixtures throughout ש״ס.

steps.title: רב made an extra decree during פסח for a different kind
steps.stepSummary: רב's normal rule needs נותן טעם for a different kind. He still forbade a משהו of חמץ in a different kind during פסח, as a גזירה because of the same kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב made a decree: חמץ during its time, mixed into a different kind, is forbidden because of a mixture with its own kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב forbids a tiny bit of חמץ in a different kind during פסח, even though his usual rule would permit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רב's general rule (step 10), a different kind is forbidden only when it gives taste. So the strict ruling during פסח is not the basic law. It is an extra rabbinic decree (גזירה), made so people won't confuse it with a same-kind mixture, which is forbidden even by a משהו.

keyTerms.meaning: not with its own kind (a different kind of food)

steps.confusionAlert: Step 10 said the ruling during פסח 'fits' רב's general view. That is only true for the same kind. For a different kind, the strict ruling is an extra decree, not the basic rule.

phrases.english: Rav made a decree
leavened bread in its time, mixed with a different kind
phrases.notes: During פסח, a tiny amount in a different kind of food

phrases.english: because of its own kind.
phrases.notes: Because a mixture with the same kind is forbidden by any amount

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב גָּזַר חָמֵץ בִּזְמַנּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִינוֹ אַטּוּ מִינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the one part of רב's ruling during פסח that step 10's general rule does not cover.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban on a different kind during פסח is a גזירה made because of the same kind.

steps.title: After פסח, the same kind is forbidden following רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב forbids a same-kind mixture after פסח because he follows רבי יהודה, who holds חמץ stays forbidden by the Torah after פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And after its time, with its own kind, it is forbidden. This follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב still forbids a tiny bit of חמץ in the same kind after פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that חמץ is still forbidden by the Torah even after פסח. Under that view it is a regular Torah prohibition. So the normal rule applies, and the same kind is forbidden by a משהו.

phrases.english: and not in its time, with its own kind, it is forbidden,
in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: He holds חמץ is forbidden by Torah law even after פסח

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁלֹּא בִּזְמַנּוֹ בְּמִינוֹ אָסוּר כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רב's ruling during פסח to his ruling after פסח.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: After פסח the same kind is forbidden because רב follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: After פסח, a different kind is permitted because there is no extra decree
steps.stepSummary: After פסח a different kind is permitted. רב did not stretch his decree that far.
steps.simpleTranslation: And with a different kind it is permitted. We do not go so far as to decree about a different kind after פסח because of its own kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב permits a tiny bit of חמץ in a different kind after פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After פסח, the normal rule says a different kind needs נותן טעם. During פסח רב added a decree because פסח is so strict. After פסח the prohibition is weaker, so he did not add that decree.

keyTerms.meaning: this far, to such an extent
we do not make a decree

steps.whatToRemember: רב: during פסח everything is forbidden (same kind by the basic law, different kind by decree). After פסח, the same kind is forbidden (like רבי יהודה), and a different kind is permitted (no decree).

phrases.english: and with a different kind, it is permitted,
because about not in its time and a different kind
because of its own kind,
we do not decree this far.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלֵּי הַאי לָא גָּזְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes explaining the last part of רב's ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No decree was made for a different kind after פסח, so it is permitted.

steps.title: שמואל's more lenient ruling on חמץ mixtures
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says: during פסח, the same kind is forbidden and a different kind is permitted. After פסח, both are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: חמץ during its time, with its own kind, is forbidden; with a different kind, permitted. After its time, whether with its own kind or a different kind, permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings שמואל's ruling on the same cases, and it is more lenient than רב's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל disagrees with רב in two places. He permits a different kind during פסח, and he permits even the same kind after פסח. The next steps explain the reason for each part.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
leavened bread in its time, with its own kind, is forbidden,
with a different kind, it is permitted.
Not in its time,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּמִינוֹ בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִינוֹ — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: whether with its own kind or a different kind, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, competing opinion to רב's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During פסח: same kind forbidden, different kind permitted. After פסח: everything permitted.

steps.title: שמואל follows his own general rule for Torah prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: שמואל forbids the same kind during פסח because of the rule he shares with רב: in every Torah prohibition, the same kind is forbidden by a משהו, and a different kind only by נותן טעם.
steps.simpleTranslation: חמץ during its time with its own kind is forbidden. שמואל follows his own reasoning, as רב and שמואל both said: all Torah prohibitions, with their own kind, are forbidden by any tiny amount; with a different kind, only when they give taste.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first part of שמואל's ruling by pointing to a general rule he holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forbidding the same kind during פסח is simply the normal rule for any Torah prohibition. The same rule also explains why a different kind is permitted when only a משהו falls in: it gives no taste.

phrases.english: leavened bread in its time, with its own kind, is forbidden:
Shmuel follows his own reasoning,
for Rav and Shmuel both say:
all prohibitions in the Torah,
with their own kind, are forbidden by any tiny amount,
with a different kind, only when they give taste.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל לְטַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first part of שמואל's ruling in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that the same kind is forbidden during פסח
steps.raayaSupportSource: The general rule of רב and שמואל on all Torah prohibitions

steps.title: שמואל made no extra decree for a different kind
steps.stepSummary: Unlike רב, שמואל did not decree against a different kind because of the same kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did not decree against a different kind because of its own kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why שמואל permits a different kind during פסח: he did not make רב's extra decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly where שמואל parts from רב (step 11). רב added a גזירה because פסח is so strict. שמואל stays with the basic rule, so a משהו in a different kind is permitted.

phrases.english: a different kind because of their own kind
he did not decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִינָן אַטּוּ מִינָן לָא גָּזַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second part of שמואל's ruling during פסח, in contrast to רב's decree.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל made no גזירה, so a different kind during פסח is permitted.

steps.title: After פסח, שמואל permits all mixtures following רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: שמואל permits both the same kind and a different kind after פסח because he follows רבי שמעון, who holds חמץ is permitted after פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: After its time, whether with their own kind or a different kind, they are permitted. This follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining שמואל by showing why he permits everything after פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that חמץ is fully permitted after פסח. Under that view there is no prohibition at all, so a mixture cannot be forbidden. This is the mirror of רב, who followed רבי יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: רב follows רבי יהודה after פסח and adds a decree during פסח. שמואל follows רבי שמעון after פסח and adds no decree. Both share the basic rule: the same kind is forbidden by a משהו, and a different kind needs נותן טעם.

phrases.english: Not in its time,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּמִינָן בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִינָן — מוּתָּרִין,
phrases.english: whether with their own kind or a different kind, they are permitted,
in accordance with Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: He holds חמץ is permitted after פסח

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּתָּרִין כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the last part of שמואל's ruling, about after פסח.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמואל permits all mixtures after פסח because he follows רבי שמעון. רב forbids the same kind because he follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's ruling on חמץ mixtures
steps.stepSummary: During פסח, both the same kind and a different kind are forbidden only by נותן טעם. After פסח, both are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: חמץ during its time (פסח), whether mixed with its own kind or with a different kind, makes the mixture forbidden only if it gives taste. Not during its time (after פסח), whether with its own kind or a different kind, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third opinion, from רבי יוחנן, about a mixture that contains חמץ. Before this, it brought the views of רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רב and שמואל, רבי יוחנן does not make the same kind stricter than a different kind during פסח. For both, the mixture is forbidden only if the חמץ adds taste. After פסח he permits everything, which matches שמואל's ruling for after פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: In its time, meaning during פסח, when חמץ is forbidden
Not in its time, meaning after פסח
With its own kind (חמץ mixed with the same type of food)
With a different kind of food
Gives taste. The mixture is forbidden only if the forbidden food can be tasted in it

steps.confusionAlert: 'Permitted after פסח' here refers to חמץ that a Jew owned during פסח and that later fell into a mixture. Do not think this is talking about חמץ that was baked after פסח, which is obviously permitted.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: חָמֵץ בִּזְמַנּוֹ, בֵּין בְּמִינוֹ וּבֵין שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִינוֹ —
phrases.english: Chametz in its time, whether with its own kind or not with its own kind,
is forbidden only when it gives taste.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא בִּזְמַנּוֹ, בֵּין בְּמִינָן בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִינָן — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: Not in its time, whether with their own kind or not with their own kind, it is permitted.
phrases.notes: After פסח, every mixture is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a third opinion, alongside רב and שמואל, on חמץ mixtures.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During פסח, the same kind and a different kind are both forbidden only by נותן טעם. After פסח, both are permitted.

steps.title: Explaining the first half: רבי יוחנן's general rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן uses נותן טעם even for the same kind because he holds, together with ריש לקיש, that every Torah prohibition is measured by נותן טעם.
steps.simpleTranslation: חמץ during its time, whether with its own kind or a different kind, is forbidden by נותן טעם. רבי יוחנן follows his own reasoning, for רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both say: all prohibitions in the Torah, whether with their own kind or a different kind, are forbidden only by נותן טעם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the source of the first half of רבי יוחנן's ruling. It shows that this half comes from his general rule for all Torah prohibitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and שמואל held that the same kind is forbidden by even a tiny amount (משהו). רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש disagree: for every Torah prohibition, the test is always taste. So there is nothing special about חמץ here. רבי יוחנן is simply applying his usual rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning, meaning consistent with a view he holds elsewhere
ריש לקיש, רבי יוחנן's study partner
Prohibitions that come from the Torah

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the opposite of the general rule of רב and שמואל (step 15). It is a basic dispute about how to measure mixtures in all of Torah law, not only for חמץ.

phrases.aramaic: חָמֵץ בִּזְמַנּוֹ, בֵּין בְּמִינוֹ בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִינוֹ
phrases.english: Chametz in its time, whether with its own kind or not with its own kind,
is forbidden when it gives taste;
Rabbi Yochanan follows his own reasoning,

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: for Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish both say:
All the prohibitions in the Torah,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּמִינָן בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִינָן — בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם.
phrases.english: whether with their own kind or not with their own kind, are forbidden when they give taste.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְטַעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This explains the first half of the ruling in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that during פסח, even the same kind is forbidden only by נותן טעם
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared rule of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש that all Torah prohibitions are measured by נותן טעם

steps.title: Explaining the second half: following רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן permits all mixtures after פסח because he follows רבי שמעון, who holds that חמץ is permitted after פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Not during its time (after פסח), whether with its own kind or a different kind, they are permitted, in accordance with רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second half of רבי יוחנן's ruling. It traces the leniency after פסח back to רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון, the prohibition on חמץ that was owned during פסח ends when פסח ends. So once פסח is over, a mixture with חמץ in it has nothing forbidden in it, no matter what kind of food it is. This matches the explanation of שמואל in step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: In accordance with רבי שמעון, who holds that חמץ owned during פסח is permitted afterward

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: during פסח, both the same kind and a different kind are forbidden only by נותן טעם (his general rule with ריש לקיש). After פסח, everything is permitted (following רבי שמעון).

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא בִּזְמַנּוֹ, בֵּין בְּמִינוֹ בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִינוֹ
phrases.english: Not in its time, whether with its own kind or not with its own kind,
they are permitted, in accordance with Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This explains the second half of the ruling in step 18, after step 19 explained the first half.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן's leniency after פסח depends on רבי שמעון's view that חמץ owned during פסח is permitted once פסח is over.
